reply_text:
*I’d hold off merging.* I found four correctness issues in `excerpt-helper` (`59856d7`) against `main`:

1. *[P1] Short bodies are truncated and always get an ellipsis* — `src/excerpt.js:6–8`  
   There’s no early return when text fits within the limit. `excerpt('hello world', 20)` returns `'hello…'`, dropping a whole word; `excerpt('hello', 20)` returns `'hello…'`, and an empty body becomes `'…'`. This contradicts the README’s unchanged-text and ellipsis rules.

2. *[P1] The helpers aren’t connected to card rendering* — `src/card.js:1–2`; new helpers in `src/excerpt.js` and `src/plain.js`  
   `card()` still returns `entry.body.trim()`. Nothing calls either new helper, so cards continue showing the full, unflattened body. If this merge is meant to enable card previews, that behavior is missing.

3. *[P2] A word ending exactly at the limit is unnecessarily discarded* — `src/words.js:2–4`  
   Slicing before searching excludes a space at index `limit`. For example, `excerpt('one two three', 7)` returns `'one…'`, although `'one two…'` preserves a complete word within the limit. The new words test actually locks in this off-by-one behavior.

4. *[P2] Markdown stripping deletes literal text characters* — `src/plain.js:3`  
   The global replacement removes underscores, asterisks, tildes, and backticks regardless of whether they’re Markdown delimiters. For example, `toPlain('snake_case and a_b_c')` returns `'snakecase and abc'`. Preview text can therefore change the meaning of ordinary identifiers and prose.

*Validation:* All four existing tests pass; I reproduced the edge cases above with direct Node calls. No files were changed.
